title: docs(adr-0020): state machine — converge to one enforced `state_machine` rule
body:
## Summary

Proposes **ADR-0020**: retire the `workflow` metadata type and `object.stateMachines`, converging the "legal status transitions" guardrail onto the single **`state_machine` validation rule** (already in use in app-showcase), and wiring it into the write path so illegal transitions are actually rejected.

Answers the recurring question *"do we still need the `workflow` metadata type?"* → **no.** Its only job was the state-machine concept, which is now the `state_machine` validation rule; its orchestration features are Flow's job (ADR-0019); and it has zero runtime enforcement today.

## What's in this PR

- **`docs/adr/0020-state-machine-converge-and-enforce.md`** (Proposed). Documents:
  - The three current declaration shapes (`workflow` type / `object.stateMachines` / `state_machine` rule) and **zero runtime enforcement** (verified: `validateRecord` reads only `fields`, never `validations`; no XState interpreter; `IWorkflowService` unimplemented).
  - The **prior-state plumbing gap** — update-path validation only gets the PATCH, not the prior record, so transition checks need the prior/merged record plumbed in (a fix that also unblocks `cross_field`/`script`).
  - AI-author naming rationale (`state_machine` matches model priors; `lifecycle` is overloaded), industry precedent (AASM / django-fsm / Dataverse / Jira), and the difference vs a Salesforce validation rule (structured introspectable transition table vs free-form formula).
- **`examples/app-showcase/src/objects/account.object.ts`** — adds an `account_lifecycle` `state_machine` rule (re-entrant topology) as a third example alongside Task/Project, and a future enforcement test fixture.

## Scope / status

Docs + example only. **No behavior change** — the implementation (retiring `workflow`, wiring write-path enforcement, rewriting app-crm `*.workflow.ts`) is tracked in the ADR's blast-radius checklist as follow-on work. Showcase typecheck passes.
